name: Albert Einstein
summary: A physicist who spoke on politics as a pacifist, internationalist and democratic socialist. He argued that unplanned capitalism concentrates power and cripples individuals, favoured a socially owned, planned economy guarded by democratic safeguards, and called for a world government holding a monopoly of armed force. He supported civil rights for Black Americans, free speech and academic freedom, a Jewish homeland in Palestine (first binational, later reconciled to Israel), and, after 1933, armed resistance to Nazi Germany.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: In 'Why Socialism?' he names the economic anarchy of capitalist society as the real source of the evil and says only a socialist, planned economy can remove it; in 1932 he wrote that the free play of economic forces will not by itself solve unemployment.

public-ownership.rationale: Writes that the way out is a socialist economy in which the means of production are owned by society itself and used in a planned fashion; in 1946-47 he also said atomic energy should stay under government control.

unions-good.rationale: Holds up the working class as a model of how organisation protected economic interests and notes that workers' long struggles won a better labour contract, urging intellectual workers to organise likewise.

property-fundamental.rationale: Argues that private ownership of the means of production concentrates power in an oligarchy of capital that democracy cannot check, and wants those means owned by society; he never treats property as a right that must be nearly inviolable.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Called for deliberate regulation of economic life by the community and, in 1947, asked why vast private corporations are allowed so much power without commensurate responsibility.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred: from his stated aim that a planned economy would guarantee a livelihood to every man, woman and child; he made no recorded comment on welfare and dependency.

central-planning.rationale: Says production should be adjusted to community needs through a planned economy, and told Soviet scientists a socialist economy's advantages outweigh its drawbacks given decent management; he warned a planned economy can also enslave the individual.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Remarked that America's prohibitive tariffs contrast oddly with its talk of international cooperation and wanted tariff barriers in Europe gradually abolished.

trade-surplus.rationale: In 1948 he said US exports would be harmless only if balanced by imports of similar value and criticised the habit of avoiding imports; he did not favour running a surplus as a goal.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Describes a planned economy that adjusts production to the community's needs, shares the work among all able to work and guarantees a livelihood to everyone.

production-for-use.rationale: Condemns capitalism because 'production is carried on for profit, not for use' and wants production adjusted to the needs of the community.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Explains that a worker's pay is set by minimum needs and labour-market competition, not by the value of what he produces, so owners take the product; he does not use the word exploitation.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: States that an extreme division of labour and a highly centralised productive apparatus are absolutely necessary in modern densely settled societies and that the idyllic self-sufficient past is gone forever.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Wrote that a successful man usually receives far more from others than corresponds to his service, and that a person's value lies in what he gives; he objected to income flowing from ownership of the means of production.

job-guarantee.rationale: Criticises capitalism for having no provision that all able and willing workers find employment and proposes an economy that distributes work among all able to work and guarantees a livelihood.

moral-incentives.rationale: Wants an education oriented to social goals that develops a sense of responsibility for fellow men in place of glorifying power and acquisitive success.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Told Soviet scientists he believed free enterprise would be unable to check chronic unemployment or keep purchasing power in balance with production, and spoke of increasingly severe depressions.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Says mankind is now a planetary community of production and consumption and that small self-sufficient units belong to a vanished past.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Argues that concentration of private capital creates an oligarchy whose power cannot be checked even by a democratic society, and that capitalists control press, radio and education.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: His case for social ownership rests on the claim that productive property should serve the needs of the community rather than the private disposal of its owners.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Calls the crippling of individuals by unlimited competition the worst evil of capitalism and criticises an education that trains pupils to worship acquisitive success.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Locates the source of economic misery in the economic anarchy of capitalist society and its institutions, not in population growth.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred: from his stated view that the means of production should be owned by society; he did not discuss water, hospitals or local transport.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Advocated a planned socialist economy under social ownership and, from 1932, community regulation of the economy, a role well beyond defence, justice and property protection.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: States that private capitalists directly or indirectly control the press, radio and education, making it extremely hard for citizens to reach objective conclusions or use political rights.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Sets as a goal that goods needed for life and health be produced with the least possible labour, and says technical progress should be organised to benefit everyone.

one-party-rule.rationale: Asks how bureaucracy can be kept from becoming all-powerful and how a democratic counterweight to it can be assured, and warns against treating a social method as a church that brands doubters traitors.

democracy-best.rationale: Praised the democratic character of American life and political constitution and backed popular election of UN delegates, but also stressed capital's hold on democracy; he never ranked democracy against other systems.

political-violence-never.rationale: From 1933 he backed armed resistance to Nazi Germany and the 1939 letter to Roosevelt, and in 1949 wrote that Israel's fighters were compelled to use force of arms to avert annihilation.

war-builds-character.rationale: Called war a mean and contemptible thing and a savage relic of barbarism that corrupts the mentality of nations.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Inferred: from his 1953 statement that ethics is an exclusively human concern with no superhuman authority, and his 1954 description of the Bible as primitive legends.

military-superiority.rationale: Said the aim of being superior to everyone else, which follows from unlimited sovereignty, poisons public life, and argued Americans are weaker, not stronger, for having the bomb.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Inferred: from his remark that Switzerland, built from several nationalities, stands at a higher stage of political development than a single-nationality state.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Says the great states of history owed their existence to conquest and that past developments were shaped by causes not exclusively economic.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Writes that egotistical drives accentuated by capitalism leave people lonely and insecure and that meaning comes only through devoting oneself to society; elsewhere calls selfish individualism a recipe for misery.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Credits science and technology with freeing people from drudgery and ending slavery in practice, while insisting new social institutions are needed to master them.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Says the seemingly idyllic time when small groups could be self-sufficient is gone forever and that division of labour and centralised production are unavoidable.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Warns against overestimating science in human problems: it supplies means but cannot create ends, and technology has brought problems of profound gravity.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Warned that treating socialism as a faith breeds fanatical intolerance and said socialism is only a framework for solving problems, not a cure-all; also called the passion over economic systems irrational.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Wrote that a planned economy can accompany the complete enslavement of the individual and that any government tends toward tyranny; of Lenin he praised the aims but did not consider his methods advisable.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Told Soviet scientists the ideological split is not what pushes the world toward war and that two capitalist, communist or monarchist powers would clash all the same; he blamed unlimited national sovereignty.

conscription.rationale: Called compulsory military service the most disgraceful symptom of lost personal dignity and in 1947 listed universal military training among the costs of accepting war.

positive-liberty.rationale: In 'On Freedom' says expression is useless to someone who must work so hard for necessities that he lacks time and strength, so a second kind of outward freedom is required.

hereditarian-race.rationale: In 'The Negro Question' calls the belief that Black Americans are inferior in intelligence or reliability a fatal misconception and traces prejudice to tradition and exploitation.

total-state.rationale: Called the modern state an idol and warned that a planned economy with control of education and information can enslave the individual.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Wrote that a nation can be called peace-loving only if it renounces any attempt to pursue interests abroad by force.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Opposed a Jewish state in 1938 and 1946, but after 1948 called Israel the fulfilment of dreams, defended it and wrote that survivors demanded the right to live on the ancient soil of their fathers.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Demanded that Palestine be thrown open to Jewish immigration within its economic capacity and backed free immigration to Israel for Jews in danger.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Says rational thinking does not suffice for our social problems and that the moral element cannot be displaced by reason; he also held science cannot supply ends.

patriotic-education.rationale: Said military and aggressively patriotic education must be abolished and condemned an inflated nationalism passing under the name of patriotism.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Argued that preparing young people for war corrupts them and called education for war a delusion; heroism by order and senseless violence he said he hated.

state-harmful.rationale: Wrote that, except for a few anarchists, everyone is convinced civilised society cannot exist without government, though any government risks sliding into tyranny.

strong-leader.rationale: Described the dictatorships of the 1930s as gangsters seizing power and poisoning youth, and warned that military-style centralisation destroys the democratic spirit.

empower-police-military.rationale: Argued in 1948 that further militarisation of the nation would slowly destroy the democratic spirit and individual dignity, and that rearmament produces the very danger it claims to answer.

experts-over-public.rationale: Says not to assume experts alone have the right to speak on how society should be organised, since socialism's ends are ethical rather than scientific.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Condemned the American habit of limiting equality and human dignity to white people and called the bias against Black Americans unworthy and fatal; he joined the NAACP.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Denounced segregation and racial discrimination in America, joined the Princeton NAACP and campaigned for equal rights.

racial-franchise.rationale: Inferred: from his statement that equality and human dignity must not be confined to one racial group and his civil-rights activism.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Called on people of good will to combat anti-Black prejudice by word and deed and acknowledged the slavery and exploitation that created it; he supported anti-lynching and civil-rights campaigns.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Wrote affidavits for European Jewish refugees and lobbied for looser US immigration rules in the 1930s and 1940s.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Urged that the UN General Assembly be strengthened above the Security Council and that UN delegates be elected directly by the people, as steps toward a supranational authority.

nation-first.rationale: Argued security is indivisible, that unlimited sovereignty condemns nations to war, and that every country should cede military force to a supranational authority.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: In 1945 he wanted a world government able to intervene where a minority oppresses a majority and said non-intervention must end.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Hoped for a politically united Europe and said anyone who wants to abolish war must back his country giving up part of its sovereignty to international institutions.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Held that a country must accept the award of an international court in disputes and that a supranational authority must have legal power to settle all conflicts.

non-intervention.rationale: Wrote that the world government should intervene in countries where a minority rules a majority and that there must be an end of non-intervention.

sacred-nation.rationale: Wrote that the true democrat can worship his nation as little as a religious person can.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Proposed denationalising military power, with national armies merged into or placed under a supranational force and only local police kept by states.

arms-reduction.rationale: Called for uncompromising support of disarmament all round and bitterly criticised the failure of disarmament conferences.

collective-defense.rationale: Described the League's collective security system as a promising step and blamed the democracies' lack of vigorous counteraction for its collapse in the face of fascist aggression.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Said in 1947 the United States must manufacture and stockpile atomic bombs to deter another nation that has them, though only for deterrence and not as an instrument of policy.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Supported force only against an enemy bent on destruction, opposed preventive war, and held that a world authority should prevent states from making war.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Stated he was not an absolute pacifist and that force is appropriate against an enemy bent on destroying him and his people; he signed the 1939 letter urging work on the atomic bomb.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Backed refusal to serve in the 1920s and early 1930s, but from 1933-34 said that refusing military service no longer helped, especially in Europe, because it weakened resistance to aggressors; the later view prevails.

multipolar-world.rationale: Argued that the anarchy of sovereign states leads inevitably to war and that real security requires a single supranational authority with a monopoly of military force.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Co-signed the 1955 manifesto asking whether mankind will end or renounce war; he elsewhere said avoiding total destruction must take priority over any other objective.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Criticised the post-war distribution of territories in Europe without regard to the wishes of the people concerned.

defeat-communism.rationale: Urged agreement with Russia on a world government, said ideological differences are not what pushes the world to war, and called for coexistence on a basis of mutual trust.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Listed the stiffening colonial policies of the Netherlands, Britain and France among the old jockeying for position that endangers peace.

indirect-election.rationale: Wanted UN delegates elected directly by the people rather than chosen by governments, so they could follow their consciences.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Valued inward freedom, meaning independence of thought from authoritarian and social prejudice, and said differences between individuals and groups should be welcomed as an enrichment.

character-from-environment.rationale: States that personality is largely formed by the environment, the structure and traditions of the society a person grows up in, while also noting biological inheritance sets a fixed constitution.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Says socialism's ends come from personalities with lofty ethical ideals that others adopt and carry forward, and that past history was shaped by non-economic causes such as conquest.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Wrote that property, outward success and luxury have always seemed to him contemptible and that worship of acquisitive success damages education and character.

simple-living.rationale: Wrote that he was strongly drawn to the simple life and uneasy about using more of other people's labour than necessary.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Held that satisfying physical needs is indispensable but not enough, and that people must be free to develop their intellectual and artistic powers.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Insisted that the individual observer's duty is not merely to wait and criticise but to serve the cause by all means, and urged intellectuals to organise politically.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Said differences between individuals and between groups should be welcomed as an enriching of existence and praised multi-national Switzerland.

party-controls-media.rationale: Declared freedom of teaching and of opinion in book and press the foundation of any people's sound development and called for it to be guaranteed by law and a spirit of tolerance.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Defended freedom of opinion and teaching, and in 1953 urged intellectuals to refuse to testify to congressional committees that suppress dissent.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Held that people must be free to develop intellectual and artistic powers and that freedom of expression in all realms of intellectual endeavour must be protected.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Signed Magnus Hirschfeld's petition against Paragraph 175 of the German criminal code.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Wrote in 1948-49 of the six million dead, the gas chambers at Maidanek and Oswiecim, and the Warsaw ghetto martyrs.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Opposed violence against animals, urged embracing all living creatures and wrote that he had eaten animal flesh with a guilty conscience.

animal-use-humane.rationale: In his last years he practised vegetarianism and wrote that man was not born to be a carnivore, so he did not simply accept animal use with minimal suffering.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Wrote in 1954 that the Bible is a collection of honourable but still primitive and rather childish legends that no interpretation can change.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Said he did not share the crusading spirit of the professional atheist and preferred humility; he opposed forcing belief or disbelief.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred: from his statement that ethics is an exclusively human concern with no superhuman authority, and his support for elected representatives.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Argued capitalists control press, radio and education and so make it very hard for citizens to judge objectively or use their political rights; he did not discuss mass culture as such.

culture-before-state.rationale: Preferred a Jewish national home and cultural community in Palestine to a state with borders, an army and temporal power, though he later accepted Israel.

corporate-influence.rationale: Argues that parties are largely financed by private capitalists who separate the electorate from the legislature, so representatives do not protect the underprivileged.

notes: His views shifted on war: in the 1920s and early 1930s he backed refusal of military service and near-absolute pacifism; from 1933 he supported armed resistance to Nazi Germany and said he was a dedicated but not absolute pacifist, and the later position is used. On Zionism he opposed a Jewish state with borders and an army (1938, 1946) but supported Israel after 1948. His 1953 advice to refuse to testify before congressional committees is cited via Wikipedia because the primary text could not be opened.
